phase_title: Deadline, Cross-Platform, and Failure Injection Hardening
scope: local Runtime durable task-state write ordering
local atomic write file fsync and parent directory sync assumptions
MCP stdio absolute deadline accounting across response wait and child-exit wait
task terminal mutation freshness checks before completion/cancel overwrite
durable write failure injection for disk-full, rename denial, and truncated temporary state
cross-platform process and directory-sync boundaries recorded without claiming unsupported hosted behavior

source_checks.requirement: TaskStore::write_task_state uses write_file_atomically instead of raw fs::write plus fs::rename.
write_file_atomically creates a sibling temporary file with create_new, writes and fsyncs the file, renames it into place, and fails closed if the Unix parent directory sync fails.
RuntimeDeadline carries an absolute expiration instant and reconstructs remaining timeout budget instead of resetting the budget between stdio response wait and child-exit wait.
stdio_request waits for the MCP child to exit only until the remaining RuntimeDeadline and then records process-tree kill evidence on timeout.
MCP stdio subprocesses run in their own Unix process group, timeout handling terminates the process tree, and timeout errors expose bounded process-tree cleanup evidence.
Runtime tests cover MCP stdio timeout cleanup and approval timeout terminalization without approval reuse.
Task terminal status updates can require expected current status and updated_at freshness before appending terminal completion or cancellation evidence.
Test-only durable write failpoints cover disk_full_before_write, truncated_state_before_rename, and rename_denied_after_sync without replacing committed state or leaking temporary files.
Unix process-group cleanup remains the enforced local process-tree implementation and non-Unix directory sync remains an explicit bounded no-op rather than claimed durability parity.

closure.summary: RRP-7.1 closes the reopened local Runtime platform/deadline/durability blocker by sharing one absolute MCP stdio deadline across response and child-exit waits, killing late-exit process trees with bounded evidence, adding checked terminal-state freshness before completion/cancel overwrites, and proving durable-write fail-closed behavior under deterministic disk-full, rename-denial, and truncated-temp failpoints.

non_goals: hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, and generic shell execution remain out of scope
direct GitHub workflow hardening remains in runtime-release-guard-ci
semantic protocol/event contract generation remains in RRP-5.1
license, publish, tag, release, and release asset decisions remain owner-controlled
runtime_release_ready remains false until the CI blocker, protocol semantic contract blocker, and owner decisions close
